# Hand-built mast: build guide

<!-- Generated by docs/make_build_docs.py from builds/hand/build_doc.csv and the CSVs beside it, common/parameters.csv, builds/hand/parameters.csv, fab/board_rules.csv and common/layout.py. Do not edit by hand: change the CSVs and rerun the script. -->

Decide, gather, drill and assemble one hand-built mast from copper-clad board, acrylic and stripboard with the 1:1 templates. The scripts, the template pages in detail and the options are in [`README.md`](README.md); the antenna choice is in [`docs/ANTENNA_SELECTION.md`](../../docs/ANTENNA_SELECTION.md). The PCB build of the same mast: [`../pcb/BUILD.md`](../pcb/BUILD.md).

Labels such as `[Pipe]` or `[No pipe]` name the options chosen under Decisions; quantities are given per option where they differ. `[All builds]` rows apply whatever you choose.

> **Firmware:** the templates are drawn for relay protocol 4 star wiring (D10 uplink TX, D0 / D1 branch RX, D7 command RX). That firmware is not written yet. See [README: Firmware and pins](README.md#firmware-and-pins-both-builds).

## Decisions before building

| # | Decision | Option | Label | What it changes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Which duck spacing? | The H50327 duck <!--p:DECK_VARIANTS-->15 mm<!--/p--> in front of each face (recommended, `docs/ANTENNA_SELECTION.md`) | `[D15]` | Drill the D15 holes on the deck template (page 1); cut the deck <!--p:DECK_DIAMETER_D15-->144 mm<!--/p--> round. |
|  |  | <!--p:DECK_VARIANTS-->31 mm<!--/p--> | `[D31]` | Drill the D31 holes; cut the deck <!--p:DECK_DIAMETER_D31-->146.3 mm<!--/p--> round. |
| 2 | Which board is the top? | The acrylic electronics plate, above the deck on M4 spacers | - | The plate's radios sit <!--p:SPACER-->27 mm<!--/p--> above the deck, on three M4 bolts in the deck's core corners. The on-deck layout is the PCB build's. |
| 3 | Will you use 1/2 in PVC pipe? | Yes: 1/2 in Sch 40 PVC (<!--p:PIPE_OD-->21.3 mm<!--/p--> OD), the pipe plate (page 2) and the stack views (page 5) | `[Pipe]` | PoE splitter and ESP32 hang on the pipe inside the core and go in through the deck's <!--p:PIPE_SAW-->2-1/4 in<!--/p--> centre hole. |
|  |  | No: the split plate (page 3) | `[No pipe]` | ESP32 and bus board hang under the plate; the PoE splitter sits in its own 4 in round box. |
|  |  | 1/2 in EMT (steel conduit) instead of the PVC pipe | `[EMT]` | <!--p:EMT_OD-->17.9 mm<!--/p--> OD, <!--p:EMT_ID-->15.8 mm<!--/p--> bore; same <!--p:ADAPTER_HOLE-->22.2 mm<!--/p--> hole for a set-screw or compression connector and locknut. Notes below. |
| 4 | How will you mount it, and to what? | Your answer: ceiling junction box, wall bracket, post, or a housing | - | With `[Pipe]`: the pipe length, the adapter, nut and cap (page 5) and the enclosure top. With `[No pipe]`: the bracket and the splitter box. Nothing for this is designed in the repo yet: write down what you choose. |
| 5 | Where are the ESP32 and the power source? | ESP32-S3-ETH and a PoE splitter (5 V USB-C out) | - | `[Pipe]`: both on the pipe. `[No pipe]`: the ESP32 under the plate, the splitter in its box. |
| 6 | Add the options? | LED direction ring (page 7) | `[LED ring]` | A WS2812B strip ring above the deck, a second pad board, its own parts list on page 7. Wiring only: the gateway does not drive it yet. |
|  |  | Unified power + LED board (page 8, pipe build) | `[Unified board]` | One stripboard in place of the bus board and the LED power board. Drawn only, not built; its wire list still shows the older wiring. |

### 1/2 in EMT instead of PVC

- **Size:** <!--p:EMT_OD-->17.9 mm<!--/p--> OD and a <!--p:EMT_ID-->15.8 mm<!--/p--> bore; the PVC pipe is <!--p:PIPE_OD-->21.3 mm<!--/p--> / <!--p:PIPE_ID-->15.8 mm<!--/p-->.
- **Mounting:** a set-screw or compression connector and locknut go in the same <!--p:ADAPTER_HOLE-->22.2 mm<!--/p--> hole.
- **RJ45:** a crimped head only just fits inside 1/2 in EMT: no boot or crimp sleeve on the plug when it goes through. Check the connector's throat too.
- **Bushings:** on every cut or drilled hole a cable passes near or through (the side slot, the tube ends), even when deburred.
- **Bonding:** bond the tube to the deck all round where it passes through: a copper collar, a ground clamp and braid, or conductive copper tape. Solder won't take on galvanized steel. Outdoors, seal the joint against zinc-copper corrosion.
- **ESP32 antenna:** in a plastic cap or insulating bushing, not on the bare steel end.

## Pages to print

From `hand_build_shield_deck_templates.pdf`; print only the pages you need.

- `[Pipe]` Pages 1 (deck), 2 (pipe plate), 4 (face, make 3), 5 (pipe stack views, older layout), 6 (star wiring).
- `[No pipe]` Pages 1, 3 (split plate), 4, 6.
- `[LED ring]` Page 7 (older layout).
- `[Unified board]` Page 8 (older wiring).
- Page 9: design formulas, reference only.

## Drill sizes

Holes you drill yourself. Counts are for one mast; the inch size is the nearest fractional drill at or just above the metric size. Don't use 1/4 in for the RP-SMA holes: the thread is 6.3 mm.

| Drill | Inch | For | `[Pipe]` | `[No pipe]` |
| --- | --- | --- | :---: | :---: |
| <!--p:HOLE_M4-->4.8 mm<!--/p--> | 3/16" | Plate: M4 bolts to the deck | 3 | 3 |
| <!--p:TIE_HOLE-->4.8 mm<!--/p--> | 3/16" | Plate: zip tie holes (pairs; any 3.0-4.8 mm hole fits a 2.5 mm tie) | 6 (3 XIAOs) | 10 (3 XIAOs + 2 across the ESP32) |
| <!--p:PLATE_M3-->3.4 mm<!--/p--> | 9/64" | Plate: bus board M3 | 1 (skip if the bus goes on the pipe) | 1 |
| <!--p:ADAPTER_HOLE-->22.2 mm<!--/p--> | 7/8" | Plate centre and enclosure top: 1/2 in male pipe adapter thread | 2 (1 plate, 1 enclosure top) | - |
| <!--p:PIPE_SAW-->2-1/4 in<!--/p--> hole saw (57 mm) | 2-1/4" | Deck centre, pipe build: splitter and ESP32 pass into the core (cuts away the M3 holes) | 1 | - |
| <!--p:ADAPTER_HOLE-->22.2 mm<!--/p--> | 7/8" | Deck centre, no pipe | - | 1 (optional) |
| <!--p:HOLE_RPSMA-->6.5 mm<!--/p--> | 17/64" | Deck: RP-SMA antenna jack, one per sector (D15, D31, P or P2) | 3 | 3 |
| <!--p:HOLE_M4-->4.8 mm<!--/p--> | 3/16" | Deck: M4 bolts in the core corners (plate spacers) | 3 | 3 |
| <!--p:COLLAR_HOLE-->3.4 mm<!--/p--> | 9/64" | Deck: M3 registration to the collar (optional, as the PCB deck) | 0 or 3 | 0 or 3 |
| <!--p:BOX_HOLE-->25 mm<!--/p--> | 1" | PoE splitter's 4 in round box | - | 1 |
| <!--p:DIPOLE_HOLE-->6.5 mm<!--/p--> | 17/64" | Face: RP-SMA bulkhead at the face centre (only for a face antenna: dipole or printed fin; page 4) | 0 or 1 per face | 0 or 1 per face |
| <!--p:HOLE_RPSMA-->6.5 mm<!--/p--> | 17/64" | Plate: antenna holes (dotted on pages 2-3, reference only) | 0 (up to 9) | 0 (up to 9) |

## Zip ties

2.5 mm wide (they fit the <!--p:TIE_HOLE-->4.8 mm<!--/p--> holes and the HS-100 mounts' slots). Lengths allow for the strap round the part plus a tail to pull on. Buy a few spares, and 2 more 150 mm ties if the pipe build's bus board goes on the pipe.

| Length | For | `[Pipe]` | `[No pipe]` |
| --- | --- | :---: | :---: |
| 100 mm (4") | Each XIAO to the plate, across its back through its hole pair | 3 | 3 |
| 100 mm (4") | Coax clamped in each 1/2 in HS-100 tie mount | 3 | 3 |
| 150 mm (6") | ESP32 to the plate, through its two hole pairs (room for standoffs) | - | 2 |
| 150 mm (6") | ESP32 to the pipe (round the pipe and board) | 2 | - |
| 200 mm (8") | PoE splitter to the pipe (round the pipe and splitter body) | 2 | - |
| | **Total** | **6 x 100, 2 x 150, 2 x 200** | **6 x 100, 2 x 150** |

## Steps

1. Print your pages at 100% ("Actual size", not "Fit to page"). Measure both 100 mm scale bars (across the top and down the left side) on each drill template before you drill: a printer can scale one direction and not the other.
1. **Deck:** drill copper-clad board from page 1, only the antenna jack you use in each sector (`[D15]` or `[D31]` for ducks, P or P2 for a patch), and cut it round. Or order a PCB deck ([`../pcb/BUILD.md`](../pcb/BUILD.md)).
1. **Plate:** lay out page 2 (`[Pipe]`) or 3 (`[No pipe]`). The layout is a suggestion: lay your own parts on the printout and check every hole against them before drilling.
1. **Drill** the plate and the faces (page 4); sizes and counts above. The plate's dotted antenna holes sit over the deck's when the M4 holes line up.
1. **Assemble** with the wiring diagram (page 6), and for `[Pipe]` the stack views (page 5).
